intro: Lesson 25: Transport in plants: xylem and phloem. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Celery practical at home with an adult (celery in coloured water for 24 h, cut across, magnifier). Draw the cross-section and label xylem; answer: 'Explain your observations.'
questions.a: Coloured dots in a ring (1); these are xylem vessels (1); water and dye moved up the xylem from the base (1)
questions.model: Teacher shows a cut celery stem on camera and labels the first coloured dot 'xylem vessel'.

questions.q: Compare transport in xylem and phloem.
questions.a: Xylem carries water and ions; phloem carries sucrose and amino acids (1); xylem one direction, phloem both (1); xylem dead hollow cells, phloem living (1)

questions.q: Aphids feed on plant sap from the stem. Which tissue do they pierce, and how could you tell?
Give two ways xylem is adapted to transport water.
questions.a: Hollow with no end walls so water flows freely (1); lignin strengthens walls so they do not collapse (1)
questions.model: Think structure then function. No end walls: continuous tube. Lignin: strong walls. Each linked to how water moves.

questions.q: Name the substances carried in phloem.

questions.a: It carries substances up and down, from sources to sinks
